assets.prompt: Handheld smartphone photograph, square-on, of a small wrought-iron monogram plate bolted to a lime-washed stone gate pillar at the top of a coastal track, mid-afternoon raking sunlight from the side. Cut into the dark iron plate is a compound family monogram: two interlocked capital letters V and C with fine serifs, enclosed inside a thin OVAL hairline rule, with a small simple ANCHOR shape beneath the letters inside the oval. The iron is dark charcoal-black but along the LOWER HALF of the plate the sunlit pale lime-washed wall behind and the sunstruck edge of the iron run close together in value, low contrast there. Realistic aged iron texture, a couple of rust spots, real bolts, faint wall texture, casual real-world snapshot, not a studio shot, sharp on the plate.

assets.defect_engineered: the mark's graphic frame is a fraction of the size the printed card suggests (the printer scaled the plate down inside a larger frame, so the recovered mark's real reproduction size is geometry inherited from the printer, readable only from the converted document); and the rate story's MINIMUM STAY run is the one a lossy mapping readout silently omits while keeping its line break, so offsets after it run short
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the retired printer's flat press PDF (travel-agent rate card) to be authored/rendered downstream.

Document: single page, 148 x 105 mm LANDSCAPE, 3 mm safety, fonts embedded. Shows a 2025 rate (a season and figure that are NOT the 2027 ones) so every field must be re-mapped.

GEOMETRY:
- GRAPHIC FRAME 1 (placed villa photograph): left ~55% of the card, full height inside margins, ~80 x 99 mm, one linked image with an integer page-item id.
- GRAPHIC FRAME 2 (placed MARK): small, top-right corner, a frame of about 34 x 34 mm into which the gate-plate mark is placed at only ~18 x 18 mm actual reproduced size (the printer scaled it down inside the larger frame), one linked image with an integer page-item id. The true reproduced size must be read from the interchange bounds, not assumed from how large the frame looks.
- TEXT FRAME A (right column, upper), one continuous story, runs:
    Run 1 (HOUSE NAME): low-contrast elegant serif, ~18 pt. Value: "Casa Oliveto"
    Run 2 (SEASON): humanist sans, ~10 pt. Value: "High Summer"
- TEXT FRAME B (right column, lower), a SEPARATE continuous story, runs in this order:
    Run 3 (NIGHTLY RATE): serif, ~15 pt. Value: "720 EUR / night"
    Run 4 (MINIMUM STAY): humanist sans, ~9.5 pt, one line. Value: "Minimum stay 7 nights"
    Run 5 (CONTACT): humanist sans, ~8.5 pt. Value: "Direct: stay@verranza.example  +39 000 000 000"

Field labels the downstream mapping must resolve (as content, not visible tokens): HOUSE, SEASON, NIGHTLY_RATE, MINIMUM_STAY, CONTACT, PHOTO, MARK.

Colours: Lime Wash #EFE9DC ground, Verranza Blue #24425A house name, Ink Charcoal #2A2925 body, Cove Water #4C7A8C hairline.

The MINIMUM STAY line (Run 4) is the run whose text content a lossy readout will drop while keeping its trailing line break; every character offset computed after it will be short by that run's length, so the minimum-stay and contact fields silently fail to become placeholders unless the story is reconstructed from the exported content runs.

assets.content:
THE THREE HOUSES, AND WHAT WE DO NOT WANT DONE TO THEM
From the owner. Verranza Coastal Retreats.

We let three houses above the cove at Punta Verranza:
- Casa Verranza, sleeps 6. The oldest, warm and simple, the one my grandfather bought.
- Casa Oliveto, sleeps 8. In the olive grove, a green terrace sail for the heat.
- Casa Scogliera, sleeps 10. On the rocks, the biggest, the best sea view. It sleeps ten, not nine, whatever the sheet says.

We sold the fourth house, Casa Fienile, last year. It is not ours to let any more and must not go to agents.

Seasons, the way we quote agents: we call them Spring, High Summer and Autumn. If the booking sheet has them as S1, S2 and S3, that is Spring, High Summer, Autumn in that order. Please put the words agents know on the cards, not the codes.

The do-not-want list, in my words: nothing cooked. No water a colour that water is not. No stone turned into a computer's idea of stone. No fake evening glow, no orange skin, no crushed blacks. Anders and I have both arrived somewhere the pictures had lied and we will not do that to a guest. A guest choosing between our own three houses should not be able to tell they were shot on different days. That is the whole job.

And the mark: the monogram the village smith cut for my grandfather is the only one there is. Give it back to us as something we can place anywhere, small on a card and reversed out of our deep blue, and still have it be ours.
